citation.title: Multi-Time Attention Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series
citation.authors: Satya Narayan Shukla; Benjamin M. Marlin

topic: Attention-based interpolation and classification for sparse, irregularly sampled multivariate time series (ICU records, human activity data)
own_question: Can learned continuous-time embeddings with time attention re-represent irregular series at reference points for interpolation and classification?
actual_method_and_evidence: A VAE encoder-decoder built on the mTAND module, evaluated on PhysioNet 2012, MIMIC-III and human-activity data with random 80/20 splits and five seeds. Encoders condition on observations from the whole window, so the evaluation is two-sided rather than causal. No plasma data.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Learned time-attention kernels have been proposed as an alternative to fixed-form similarity kernels for interpolating irregularly sampled series.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a general machine-learning method. It was not applied to CES, BES or ECEI and was not tested in a strictly causal setting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The models use time points observed across the full window, so they are not current-report nowcasts from strictly past inputs. Report arrival times were not modeled.
validation_if_relevant: Random splits with seed repeats. The source defines no temporal or campaign-level held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite this paper as evidence of fusion or CES performance.
Do not treat its speed results as evidence about our 10 ms computation budget.
Do not claim we implemented mTAN.
Do not infer that its results transfer to causal settings.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most an optional background citation for learned irregular-time interpolation. It is not needed for the CES nowcasting framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
